sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
Memory Management - Comprehensive Examples

```python
"""
Memory Management - Comprehensive Examples
==========================================
"""

import sys
import gc
import weakref
import array
from collections import deque

print("=" * 70)
print("MEMORY MANAGEMENT EXAMPLES")
print("=" * 70)

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 1: Reference Counting
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 1: Reference Counting")
print("=" * 70)

# Create object
x = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
print(
    f"Initial ref count: {sys.getrefcount(x) - 1}"
)  # -1 for getrefcount's temp reference

# Create more references
y = x
z = x
print(f"After creating y and z: {sys.getrefcount(x) - 1}")

# Delete references
del y
print(f"After deleting y: {sys.getrefcount(x) - 1}")

del z
print(f"After deleting z: {sys.getrefcount(x) - 1}")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 2: Object Size Comparison
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 2: Object Size Comparison")
print("=" * 70)

# Different data types
data = {
    "int": 42,
    "float": 3.14,
    "string": "hello world",
    "list": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5],
    "tuple": (1, 2, 3, 4, 5),
    "dict": {"a": 1, "b": 2, "c": 3},
    "set": {1, 2, 3, 4, 5},
}

print("Memory size of different types:")
for name, obj in data.items():
    size = sys.getsizeof(obj)
    print(f"  {name:10s}: {size:4d} bytes")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 3: Using __slots__ for Memory Efficiency
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 3: Using __slots__ for Memory Efficiency")
print("=" * 70)
```

sections.title: class SlottedPoint
sections.body:
```python
# With __slots__
class SlottedPoint:
    __slots__ = ["x", "y"]

    def __init__(self, x, y):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y

# Create instances
regular = RegularPoint(10, 20)
slotted = SlottedPoint(10, 20)

# Compare sizes
regular_size = sys.getsizeof(regular) + sys.getsizeof(regular.__dict__)
slotted_size = sys.getsizeof(slotted)

print(f"Regular class: {regular_size} bytes")
print(f"Slotted class: {slotted_size} bytes")
print(
    f"Memory saved: {regular_size - slotted_size} bytes ({(1 - slotted_size/regular_size)*100:.1f}%)"
)

# Create many instances to see the difference
n = 10000
regular_list = [RegularPoint(i, i) for i in range(n)]
slotted_list = [SlottedPoint(i, i) for i in range(n)]

regular_total = sum(sys.getsizeof(p) + sys.getsizeof(p.__dict__) for p in regular_list)
slotted_total = sum(sys.getsizeof(p) for p in slotted_list)

print(f"\nFor {n} instances:")
print(f"Regular: {regular_total / 1024:.2f} KB")
print(f"Slotted: {slotted_total / 1024:.2f} KB")
print(f"Saved: {(regular_total - slotted_total) / 1024:.2f} KB")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 4: Generators vs Lists Memory Usage
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 4: Generators vs Lists Memory Usage")
print("=" * 70)

n = 100000

# List comprehension - all in memory
list_squares = [x**2 for x in range(n)]
list_size = sys.getsizeof(list_squares)

# Generator - computed on demand
gen_squares = (x**2 for x in range(n))
gen_size = sys.getsizeof(gen_squares)

print(f"List of {n} squares: {list_size / 1024:.2f} KB")
print(f"Generator: {gen_size} bytes")
print(f"Memory ratio: {list_size / gen_size:.0f}x")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 5: Garbage Collection
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 5: Garbage Collection")
print("=" * 70)

# Check garbage collection status
print(f"GC enabled: {gc.isenabled()}")
print(f"GC counts (gen0, gen1, gen2): {gc.get_count()}")
```

# Create circular reference
class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.next = None

    def __del__(self):
        print(f"  Node {self.value} deleted")

# Create circular reference
node1 = Node(1)
node2 = Node(2)
node1.next = node2
node2.next = node1

print("\nCreated circular reference")
print(f"Ref count node1: {sys.getrefcount(node1) - 1}")
print(f"Ref count node2: {sys.getrefcount(node2) - 1}")

# Delete references
del node1
del node2
print("Deleted node1 and node2 references")

# Manual garbage collection
print("Running garbage collector...")
collected = gc.collect()
print(f"Collected {collected} objects")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 6: Weak References

print("\n" + "=" * 70)

sections.title: class LargeObject
sections.body:
```python
class LargeObject:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name
        self.data = [0] * 1000  # Simulate large object

    def __del__(self):
        print(f"  {self.name} being deleted")

# Strong reference
obj = LargeObject("Strong")
print(f"Strong ref count: {sys.getrefcount(obj) - 1}")

# Weak reference doesn't increase ref count
weak_obj = weakref.ref(obj)
print(f"After weak ref: {sys.getrefcount(obj) - 1}")
print(f"Weak ref alive: {weak_obj() is not None}")

# Delete strong reference
print("Deleting strong reference...")
del obj

# Weak reference now returns None
print(f"Weak ref after deletion: {weak_obj()}")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 7: Array Module for Numeric Data
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 7: Array Module for Numeric Data")
print("=" * 70)

n = 10000

# List of integers
int_list = list(range(n))
list_size = sys.getsizeof(int_list)

# Array of integers
int_array = array.array("i", range(n))
array_size = sys.getsizeof(int_array)

print(f"List of {n} integers: {list_size / 1024:.2f} KB")
print(f"Array of {n} integers: {array_size / 1024:.2f} KB")
print(
    f"Memory saved: {(list_size - array_size) / 1024:.2f} KB ({(1 - array_size/list_size)*100:.1f}%)"
)

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 8: String Interning
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 8: String Interning")
print("=" * 70)

# Small strings are automatically interned
a = "hello"
b = "hello"
print(f"'hello' interned: {a is b}")

# Strings with special characters might not be
c = "hello world!"
d = "hello world!"
print(f"'hello world!' interned: {c is d}")

# Force interning
e = sys.intern("hello world!")
f = sys.intern("hello world!")
print(f"Force interned: {e is f}")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 9: Memory Profiling with tracemalloc
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 9: Memory Profiling with tracemalloc")
print("=" * 70)

import tracemalloc

# Start tracking
tracemalloc.start()

# Allocate memory
data1 = [i for i in range(10000)]
data2 = [i**2 for i in range(10000)]
data3 = {i: i**2 for i in range(10000)}

# Get memory statistics
current, peak = tracemalloc.get_traced_memory()
print(f"Current memory usage: {current / 1024:.2f} KB")
print(f"Peak memory usage: {peak / 1024:.2f} KB")

# Stop tracking
tracemalloc.stop()

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 10: Context Manager for Resource Management
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 10: Context Manager for Resource Management")
print("=" * 70)
```

sections.body:
Load all data into memory Process data incrementally

```python
class ManagedResource:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name

    def __enter__(self):
        print(f"  Acquiring {self.name}")
        return self

    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
        print(f"  Releasing {self.name}")
        return False

# Proper resource management
print("Using context manager:")
with ManagedResource("Database Connection") as resource:
    print(f"  Using {resource.name}")
print("Resource automatically released")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 11: Memory-Efficient Data Processing
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 11: Memory-Efficient Data Processing")
print("=" * 70)

def process_large_data_bad(n):
    """Load all data into memory"""
    data = [i**2 for i in range(n)]
    return sum(data)

def process_large_data_good(n):
    """Process data incrementally"""
    return sum(i**2 for i in range(n))

n = 100000

# Bad way - stores all
import tracemalloc

tracemalloc.start()
result1 = process_large_data_bad(n)
current1, peak1 = tracemalloc.get_traced_memory()
tracemalloc.stop()

# Good way - generator
tracemalloc.start()
result2 = process_large_data_good(n)
current2, peak2 = tracemalloc.get_traced_memory()
tracemalloc.stop()

print(f"Bad approach peak memory: {peak1 / 1024:.2f} KB")
print(f"Good approach peak memory: {peak2 / 1024:.2f} KB")
print(f"Memory saved: {(peak1 - peak2) / 1024:.2f} KB")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 12: Object Pooling Pattern
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 12: Object Pooling Pattern")
print("=" * 70)
```

sections.title: class ObjectPool, class ExpensiveObject
sections.body:
Get object from pool

```python
class ObjectPool:
    def __init__(self, factory, size=10):
        self.factory = factory
        self.pool = deque([factory() for _ in range(size)])
        self.in_use = set()

    def acquire(self):
        """Get object from pool"""
        if self.pool:
            obj = self.pool.popleft()
        else:
            obj = self.factory()
        self.in_use.add(id(obj))
        return obj

    def release(self, obj):
        """Return object to pool"""
        if id(obj) in self.in_use:
            self.in_use.remove(id(obj))
            self.pool.append(obj)

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.pool)

class ExpensiveObject:
    def __init__(self):
        self.data = [0] * 1000  # Simulate expensive creation

# Create pool
pool = ObjectPool(ExpensiveObject, size=5)
print(f"Pool initialized with {len(pool)} objects")

# Acquire objects
obj1 = pool.acquire()
obj2 = pool.acquire()
print(f"After acquiring 2: {len(pool)} objects in pool")

# Release objects
pool.release(obj1)
pool.release(obj2)
print(f"After releasing 2: {len(pool)} objects in pool")

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("All examples completed!")
print("=" * 70)
```
